approximations: Interconnect energy uses Timeloop's Legacy network model with one shared 45nm wire constant and per-architecture switching terms (archs/_shared/noc.yaml); hop distance is derived by Timeloop from each level's Accelergy area. The recon arm scales the WEIGHT share of NoC energy by K/N like the other on-chip categories.
exact stored codeword count x measured DRAM refetch factor; parity + message padding; rounded up to whole DRAM words once

The baseline's DRAM cost is a PER-BIT PRICE, not extra traffic: it reads the same weight bits as the embedded arm (the decoder is on the DRAM die, so parity is corrected there and never crosses the datapath) and pays 22 pJ/bit against 20 for the bigger, indexed array (x1.1000 on the whole DRAM category, weights, inputs and outputs alike -- a per-bit cost is a property of the device, not of a dataspace). The parity accounting on this result is the array-SIZE evidence for that price, not an energy term; it charges no pJ. E_background and E_refresh grow with the array and are not modelled.

facts.label: Eyeriss v1 (+8kB filter GLB)
facts.citation: Same JSSC 52(1), 2017 as eyeriss_like.  Differs from it in ONE block: the 8 kB filter allocation the paper describes -- "the remaining 8 kB (two banks of 512-b x 64-b SRAMs) of the GLB is allocated for filter weights to compensate for insufficient off-chip traffic bandwidth" -- is declared as a Timeloop storage level instead of !Nothing. Unlike eyeriss_v2_like_wglb, whose weight level is NOT in its paper, this level IS published; what is uncertain is whether a prefetch buffer should be modelled as a reuse level.  The pair BRACKETS that uncertainty: eyeriss_like is the upper bound on DRAM weight traffic (and so on the ECC saving), eyeriss_like_wglb the lower bound. Quote the pair, never one alone.

provenance.source_document: Chen, Krishna, Emer, Sze, IEEE JSSC 52(1), 2017 -- same paper as eyeriss_like

filter_glb.quote: "Even though it is not required by the dataflow, the remaining 8 kB (two banks of 512-b x 64-b SRAMs) of the GLB is allocated for filter weights to compensate for insufficient off-chip traffic bandwidth. While the PE array is working on a processing pass, the GLB preloads the filters used by the next processing pass."
filter_glb.modelled: depth 256 (2 x 128), width 64, n_banks 2, datawidth 8 -> 2048 weights
filter_glb.divergence: THE PAPER'S 8 kB IS depth 1024. This file declares 256 -- 2 kB, a QUARTER of the published allocation. The entry count arrived in commit 3a770cc (2026-09-11) with no note, and this field went on saying 1024 until 2026-09-13. CONFIRMED AND KEPT on 2026-09-13 (prompt_7 C1.7, the user's decision): the cold pass runs on the declared geometry. The BANK SHAPE (64-b words, 2 banks) is the paper's, so the per-access energy is the right array; only the depth is this study's.
filter_glb.rationale: The BANK GEOMETRY is published exactly and the CAPACITY is not modelled at the published value (above); what is separately a judgement call is whether a double-buffered prefetch store should be declared as a Timeloop reuse level. Modelled as a reuse level here and as !Nothing in eyeriss_like, so the two BRACKET the answer instead of one of them silently choosing it -- with the 2 kB declaration making this end of the bracket LOOSER than the published 8 kB would.
filter_glb.why_it_matters: eyeriss_like refetches resnet18's weights 7.0x from DRAM against 1.0-2.3x for every other design, and the ECC saving is very nearly 0.3125 * E_dram_weights / (total + 0.3125 * E_dram_weights). So this single structural choice sets the largest saving in the study. It is the reason this variant exists. Boundary R2's ENTIRE saving rides on this level, and since prompt_7 C1.3 so does the fc-layer latency term.

weights_spad.quote: "the filter spad is implemented in a 224-b x 16-b SRAM due to its large size" (JSSC 2017 Sec. V-B)
weights_spad.modelled: depth 16, width 16, datawidth 8 -> 32 weights/PE, 5,376 on chip
weights_spad.divergence: THE PAPER'S ARRAY IS depth 224 = 448 8-bit weights per PE. This file declares 16 = 32 weights, a FOURTEENTH. Same commit and same decision as filter_glb above. Consequence, recorded in prompt_5 and in legacy/FINDINGS_detail_2026-09-11.md: THE WIDTH TABLE renormalises 256 bits to depth 3 at width 96 (+12.5%), which is barely a reuse level, and the per-code spread it leaves in the 8-bit reference arm is what once made BCH(63,39) read as a 37.69% win that was really the reference falling off a tiling cliff. archs/eyeriss_like/arch_paper.yaml still declares 224, so the two v1 files do NOT declare the same PE.
weights_spad.why_it_matters: Boundary R5a is the only bar that narrows this level, so its saving and its feasibility (`G_rec` against the resident tile) both ride on a capacity that is not the published one.

psum_glb.quote: "100 kB of the GLB is allocated for ifmaps and psums ... divided into 25 banks, each of which is a 512-b x 64-b (4 kB) SRAM" (JSSC 2017 Sec. V-A)
psum_glb.divergence: 12 BANKS OF 512 ENTRIES IS depth 6144; this file declares 6656, which is 13 banks' worth of entries spread over the 12 banks it declares (554.67 each), so the GLB totals 27 of its 25 banks. Raised from 6144 on 2026-09-13 (the user's decision, testing a larger psum store); the comments in the arch file said 6144 for about forty minutes until this entry and they were corrected, not the number. n_banks is what reaches CACTI, so the per-access energy is still a 512 x 64b bank; only the entry count is this study's.
psum_glb.why_it_matters: Partial sums are not a dataspace reconstruction touches, so no ECC percentage moves with it -- but psum_glb is a large share of on-chip energy under ECC_OPT_METRIC=edp, so it moves every bar's DENOMINATOR and with it every percentage in the figure. And it is in arch_fingerprint(), so changing it re-maps the whole study.

psum_spad.divergence: THE PAPER'S ARRAY IS depth 24; the stock example design declares 16; this file declared 64 until 2026-09-13 and now declares 96. The 64 came in with filter_glb and weights_spad above; the 96 is a separate and later decision (the user's, 2026-09-13, testing a larger psum store). It holds partial sums, which reconstruction never touches, so it moves no ECC percentage -- but it is 4x the published register file and the design must not be quoted as the published PE because of it.

mapper_settings.seed_note: timeloop-mapper v4 exposes no random seed; pytimeloop's Mapper spec has no `random_seed` attribute. ECC_MAPPER_SEED is RECORDED so a result says which value was asked for, but it does not make the search deterministic. What does bound it is the thread count and victory condition, both of which are in the fingerprint -- so pin ECC_MAPPER_THREADS for a reproducible run rather than leaving it at 'all cores', which differs per machine.
